newsitem.title: UK: HSBC up again as stock shortage continues.
newsitem.headline: HSBC up again as stock shortage continues.

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc showed no sign of running out of steam in early trade on Thursday as the Anglo-Hong Kong banking group continued to lead the bank sector and the FTSE-100 index into record territory.

Dealers attributed the gains to a contined shortage of stock in the market as institutions attempt to build weightings in the bank sector, which has expanded this year with the flotation of former building societies such as Halifax Plc.
"It's just crazy stuff, I've been dealing in bank stocks for years and I've never had such a busy time," said one head of equity trading. "It's just unbelieveable."

HSBC shares were up 64p at a record 22.15 stg by 0805 GMT and other bank stocks also rose, with Barclays Plc up 26-1/2 at 13.09 stg, National Westminster Bank Plc up 11p at 885 and Lloyds TSB Group Plc 16-1/2p higher at 733. Abbey National Plc gained 17p at 896-1/2.

The sharp rise in bank stocks this year had been one of the prime motors behind the record-breaking run in the FTSE 100 index, which on Thursday carried the blue chip stock index to within a whisker of the 5,000 level.
Yet dealers and investors have been left shocked by the persistance of the sector's strength.

"It is just mad, people are scared to sell it," said another dealer. "It is just a markup and no-one wants to sell...institutions are still trying to weight up and the way things are going they will achieve that without having to buy more."
Dealers were reluctant to call a top in HSBC or other bank stocks.
"HSBC will continue strong as long as Hong Kong holds up and the whole financial sector is in demand," said one.
